answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake in a kernel registry before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when an identity is proven to have double-claimed a reward. A crystal-clear audit trail links claims to one locked stake, while a ridge of independent reviewers checks disputes before slashing. Spawning a thousand sybils no longer creates free influence: the attacker must acquire and immobilize a thousand stakes, pay opportunity cost, and risk losing them if caught.
